# dsh-paste-collapse

Collapse a large paste in the DeepSeek Harness composer into a Codex style
placeholder, show a pill

for it, and expand it back to the full text on the
host right before the model reads the turn.

The model still sees every character you pasted. Nothing is written to disk and
no tokens are saved

— the placeholder is a display convenience, not a
compression.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## The rules (the same ones Codex uses)

| Threshold | 1000 characters (`LARGE_PASTE_CHAR_THRESHOLD` in Codex) |
| Placeholder | `[Pasted Con

tent 12000 chars]` |
| A second paste of the same size | `[Pasted Content 12000 chars] #2`, then `#3

`, … |
| The counter | per size: a 3000 character paste starts its own sequence |
| Expansion | FIFO

: the first occurrence of a placeholder gets the first text |
| A placeholder without a text | left
alone, sent to the model as it is |

The placeholder text, the numbering and the FIFO expansion are a port of
Codex (`codex-rs/tui/src/bo

ttom_pane/chat_composer.rs`): `next_large_paste_placeholder`
and `expand_pending_pastes`.
## The pill
Every collapsed paste gets a pill on the top edge of the composer:

* the first line of the pasted text, cut to 16 characters
* the number of characters, shortened (`6.

7k` instead of `6684`)
* click it to open the full text in a side panel

The side panel is the drawer Codex and WorkBuddy use: the whole text, the
character count, a copy bu

tton and a close button. `Esc` or a click outside
closes it.

The pill uses the DSH native colours (CSS variables only, no hard coded hex),
so it follows the ligh
t and the dark theme.
## The sent message shows a pill

The turn you already sent shows the collapsed paste as a pill as well, instead
of a wall of text: th

e bubble renders the pasted text as a small chip with the
preview and the character count, and click

ing it opens the same side panel
with the whole text.

The bubble asks the client first and the host second, so a message still shows
its pill after the cl

ient lost its copy (after a restart, for example). When
neither of them has the text any more, the m

essage simply shows the plain
text.
### Two things worth knowing about the pill in a message

**The bubble carries the expanded text, not the placeholder.** The host swaps
the placeholder back f

or the full text in `agent/pre-step`, and that expanded
text is what the session stores and what the

bubble shows. The pill is
therefore found by looking for *the pasted text the client remembers* ins

ide
the message. When neither the client nor the host holds that text any more —
after a host restar
t, for example — the message falls back to the plain text.

**The slot is won, not negotiated.** The host renders the text of a user
message with the `text` key

of the `conversation.user.text.node` slot, and
this plugin takes that seat. In the browser the prio

rity is allocated by the
`cordis-client-runner` facade (`guard.ts`, `allocatePriority()`), and a plu

gin
half that registers later naturally gets the lower priority — so it wins over
the host's 100. Th

e `priority: 50` this plugin passes explicitly only really
takes effect on the static bundled path.

Both paths win, but that is a
precondition, not a coincidence: do not rely on being able to reorder

t that is a
precondition, not a coincidence: do not rely on being able to reorder the
registrations.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Use the `github:` form: this plugin is not published to npm, and the name
`dsh-paste-collapse` on np
m belongs to a different author's package.
or link a checkout:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The plugin has two halves: the host half (`lib/index.js`) and the client half
(`client.js`). The cli

ent half is what turns the paste into a placeholder, the
host half is what expands it again.
## Limits

* **The text only lives in memory.** The host keeps the pasted texts in a
plain array. Nothing is wr

itten to disk, nothing is uploaded, and the texts
are gone when the host process ends.
* **After a h

ost restart the text is lost.** The placeholder stays in the
composer, but the host no longer knows

the text, so the placeholder is sent
to the model as it is. The pill marks this state as *text lost*

.
* **No token saving.** The model reads the full text, exactly as if you had
pasted it directly. Th

e plugin only makes the composer readable.
* **A paste is only collapsed when the host answers.** Th

e host is asked twice
and every attempt waits up to 5 seconds, so the paste waits at most 10
seconds

. When the host still does not answer, the text is inserted as it
is — the paste is never lost.
* **

A placeholder the user deletes is dropped.** The client tells the host, and
the host forgets the tex

t once the turn has had its chance to use it — so
the next paste of the same size starts at the bare

placeholder again.
* **A submitted turn keeps its text.** The composer clears the draft when the
tu

rn is sent, and the expansion on the host runs after that. The text
therefore survives the clear: th

e model reads the full text, not the
placeholder.
* **The texts are forgotten one by one.** The host

keeps the 50 newest texts
it delivered and the client keeps the 100 newest texts it sent; the two
l

imits are independent. Older ones are dropped, and the message that held
one falls back to the plain

are independent. Older ones are dropped, and the message that held
one falls back to the plain text.
## Differences from Codex
Only two:

1. **When the expansion happens.** Codex expands the placeholder in the
composer, DSH expands it on

the host in `agent/pre-step`, right before the
model reads the turn.
2. **How the placeholder looks.

** Codex shows plain text, DSH shows the same
placeholder plus a pill.
## Tests
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`test/client-bundle.mjs` runs `client.js` inside a fake window with a fake
React and a fake DOM, so

the composer behaviour is tested without a browser.
`selftest/host-e2e.mjs` runs the host plugin aga

inst a fake Cordis context and
uses a temporary `DSH_HOME`.
See VERIFY.md for the full acceptance checklist.
